name: Jean Shen
life: “I still remember taking pictures on the day nobody remembered the camera.” People around Tideline Market know Jean by a small Monday habit. Jean picks out the bruised fruit first and asks the seller what will ripen by supper.
voice: I took a photograph because it looked like our street under the one snowfall I remember.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a gray fisher's sweater and a replacement button a shade darker than the others. Jean has an aquiline nose and a square chin, with dark brown curls cut close behind the ears. Jean squares up pieces of paper while thinking during a conversation.
personality: Likes beautiful, unnecessary things and gets cross with people who mistake poverty for a lack of taste. Jean takes longer choosing a cheap birthday card than an expensive coat.
agenda: To print a picture of the white crystals.
family: Galen Howe is Jean’s cousin raised in the same household. Jean chooses whether to use it. Galen saves a place. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *Ten fingers*, Galen says, “We used to compete for the same corner lease.”
connections: Desmond Baldwin. The photograph of the white table picks up a small embroidered fish.

reactions.situation: An employer wants every coat returned before supper
reactions.response: Jean asks the employer which garments are actually needed for tonight's shift.

reactions.situation: A stranger waves a phone camera in a crying person's face
reactions.response: Jean asks the filmer to lower the phone and gets another familiar face to stand by the person crying.

reactions.situation: When a relative dismisses a little luxury
reactions.response: Jean asks which ordinary pleasure the relative would give up first.
